newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Profit takers moved into the Dutch bond market on Friday, firmly shutting the door on the possibility of a fourth successive daily rise in prices.
Bonds finished lower across the yield curve, particularly at the longer end, as the the 30 basis point fall in 10-year yields over the last month proved too tempting for sellers.
Dealers said the benchmark long bond, the Jan 2023, was hit hardest, with retail accounts unloading their holdings and institutions swapping into bunds, which are seen as cheaper.
"There's no buyers. People think it's too long a maturity," said one dealer.
Lower September U.S. consumer sentiment was shrugged off.
A dealer said guilder bonds followed the downward path of bunds, which weakened to test 98.75 support several times, but the fall in guilder bonds was on little volume.
"The problem is that Holland is expensive to go into. It's expensive for fundamental reasons," he said.
But another trader was more bullish, attributing the sell-off to end-of-quarter book squaring and saying he expected the yield discount to bunds to widen next week.
"Maybe it's time to pick up some again," he added.
